newsitem.title: CUBA: Despite U.S. embargo, Cuban tourism climbs.
newsitem.headline: Despite U.S. embargo, Cuban tourism climbs.

text.p: About 1.2 million tourists are expected to visit Cuba this year, 21 per cent more than in 1996, despite Washington's policy of discouraging foreigners from doing business with Havana, Vice Minister of Tourism Eduardo Rodriguez de la Vega said on Monday.

He told a news conference that Italy provided more than 10% of the tourists to Cuba followed by Canada, Spain, France, Germany, Mexico and Britain. All of those nations are on record as strongly condemning the 35-year-old U.S. embargo on trade with communist-ruled Cuba.
Rodriguez de la Vega said that so far this year the 1997 tourism forecast was 90.5 per cent on track. He said the goal for the year 2000 was two million tourists.
During the decades following Fidel Castro's revolution in 1959, Cuba showed little interest in developing its tourism industry for foreigners. In 1990, 330,000 tourists visited Cuba.
It was only since the 1991 breakup of its main benefactor, the Soviet Union, that the island-nation has given priority to tourism as a way of shoring up its hard-hit economy.

Since then, Castro's government, which refuses to renounce socialism, has encouraged investments by foreign capitalists in joint ventures with Cuban enterprises. Dozens of new hotels with tens of thousands of rooms have been built.
